_source: v1.1 (Decision 35) seed: the 115 CDP 2023 controlled action labels (adaptbase-core cdp_solution_crosswalk.json; every label is a concept or an alias), the Solution names reused by two or more plans in the graph on 2026-10-01 (adaptbase-core#321 §2.6 d), and solution-categories subcategories that name a concrete intervention.
_usage: Solution.concept_id. Each concept carries the category_id, subcategory_id and ipcc_action_types that the seeder copies onto the Solution node; extraction never writes those three.
_review: Reviewed 2026-10-06 (Anthony; the remaining rows were settled on the reviewer's rule 'if we can't classify it more narrowly, we shouldn't record it'). Decision 35 records the outcome. unmapped_cdp_labels are CDP controlled labels that deliberately map to no concept: a CDP action carrying only those gets no IMPLEMENTS edge.
_revision_plan: Provisional until the plan corpus is fully extracted. Once every plan in the corpus has been extracted, review this list again against what plans actually prescribe: the concepts proposed through the queue, Solutions left without a concept_id, the dropped umbrellas (green infrastructure, urban greening, ecosystem-based adaptation) and the unmapped CDP labels. Revise it in one versioned pass (decisions-log entry, ontology version bump). Tracked in README > Future ontology improvements.
_note: Governed, growing list: closed to the extractor (a class not on the list is emitted with proposed: true and reviewed), open through the proposal queue. New concepts arrive as a PR to this file with added_in set; deprecation keeps the id with status: deprecated and replaced_by. cdp_labels records which CDP controlled labels fold into the concept, for the CDP import. aliases are identity-grade synonyms for the resolver.

concepts.name: Sea wall

cdp_labels: Sea walls and coastal protection structures

concepts.name: Levee

concepts.name: Hydrological and flood modelling

concepts.name: Integrated water resource management

concepts.name: Water quality monitoring

concepts.name: Reef restoration

concepts.name: Building floodproofing

concepts.name: Emergency shelter

concepts.name: Climate-sensitive disease surveillance and prevention

Land zoning laws to increase local food access (including grocery stores, farmers markets, community gardens, etc.)

concepts.name: Efficient irrigation

concepts.name: Urban heat mapping

concepts.name: Hazard mapping

concepts.name: Climate and environmental monitoring

concepts.name: Climate projections and downscaling

concepts.name: Wildfire detection and suppression

concepts.name: Emergency response capacity

concepts.name: Informal settlement upgrading

concepts.name: Adaptive land-use planning and management

concepts.name: Community-based natural resource management

concepts.name: Payments for ecosystem services

concepts.name: Species and genetic conservation
concepts.definition: Protecting species and genetic diversity at risk from climate change, in place or by relocation and storage.
cdp_labels: Ex situ conservation and seed banks

concepts.name: Urban green space
concepts.definition: Creating, expanding, improving or protecting parks and other vegetated open spaces within the built-up area to provide cooling, infiltration, flood storage and recreation.

concepts.name: Drought-tolerant landscaping
concepts.definition: Replacing irrigated lawns and ornamental plantings with native, drought-adapted or low-water vegetation and surfaces that need little or no irrigation.

concepts.name: Seismic retrofit
aliases: Seismic retrofit of unreinforced masonry buildings
concepts.definition: Strengthening existing buildings and structures so they resist earthquake shaking and collapse, addressing a geophysical rather than climate hazard.

concepts.name: Depaving
aliases: Depaving and greening of hard surfaces
concepts.definition: Removing, narrowing or avoiding sealed surfaces and replacing them with soil and vegetation so that rain infiltrates and ground surfaces stay cooler.

concepts.name: Public drinking water point
concepts.definition: Free drinking fountains or refill stations in public spaces that help people stay hydrated during hot weather.

concepts.name: Green wall
concepts.definition: Vegetation grown on building facades or vertical structures to cool surfaces, insulate buildings and manage runoff.

concepts.name: Stormwater infiltration system
concepts.definition: A buried trench, soakaway, well or borehole filled with gravel or open to the soil that receives stormwater runoff and lets it infiltrate into the ground.

concepts.name: District cooling
concepts.definition: A centralised plant and pipe network that produces chilled water and distributes it to multiple buildings for space cooling.

concepts.name: Critical facility hardening

concepts.definition: Retrofitting, flood-proofing, weatherproofing and adding redundancy to critical facilities and networks so they keep operating through hazard events.

concepts.name: Business continuity planning
concepts.definition: Plans, assessments and support that help businesses, organisations and essential services keep operating through hazard events and recover afterwards.

concepts.name: Vacant lot greening
aliases: Vacant lot and public space reclamation
concepts.definition: Converting a vacant or underused lot into a small vegetated public open space that provides shade, cooling and infiltration.

concepts.name: Professional resilience training
concepts.definition: Training and knowledge programmes that build the skills of officials, practitioners and utility operators to plan and deliver climate adaptation.

concepts.name: Deployable flood barrier
concepts.definition: A temporary or demountable barrier erected along streets, buildings or riverbanks when flooding is forecast and removed afterwards.

concepts.name: Climate risk and vulnerability assessment
concepts.definition: A systematic assessment of how exposed, sensitive and adaptive a place, its services, buildings and infrastructure are to climate hazards, used to set adaptation priorities.

concepts.name: Climate-resilient public space
concepts.definition: Designing parks, plazas and streets so they manage heat and store or slow floodwater while remaining usable during extreme conditions.

concepts.name: Green street
concepts.definition: A street retrofitted with trees, planted swales, permeable surfaces and subsurface storage that capture runoff and provide shade.

concepts.name: Resilient construction workforce training
concepts.definition: Training and accrediting builders, tradespeople, engineers and inspectors so that hazard-resistant construction and retrofit standards are applied in practice.

concepts.name: Real-time stormwater control
aliases: Remote monitoring and automated control of flood structures
concepts.definition: Remote monitoring and automated or managed operation of gates, weirs, pumps and drainage control levels to regulate stormwater and floodwater as conditions change.

concepts.name: Occupational heat protection standard
concepts.definition: Rules and workplace practices such as rest, shade, hydration and work-pause requirements that protect indoor and outdoor workers from heat stress.

concepts.name: Heat-adaptive scheduling
concepts.definition: Shifting the timing, location or format of outdoor work, school, recreation and public activities to avoid the hottest periods of the day or season.

concepts.name: Participatory monitoring
concepts.definition: Residents and volunteers collecting and sharing environmental and hazard observations that feed into monitoring, early warning and planning.

concepts.name: Cool route
concepts.definition: A designated pedestrian or cycling route, or connected network of routes, lined with shade, vegetation, water and rest points so people can move safely during heat.

concepts.name: Drainage maintenance
aliases: Street sweeping and drain inlet maintenance
concepts.definition: Routine inspection, cleaning and upkeep of drains, gullies, inlets, culverts and other stormwater assets so the network retains its design capacity during storms.

concepts.name: Climate risk screening
aliases: Climate risk screening of capital projects
concepts.definition: A tool or procedure that checks proposed projects, assets or investments against climate hazards and resilience criteria before they are approved or funded.

concepts.name: Climate risk modelling
concepts.definition: Data-driven analytics that combine hazard, exposure and vulnerability information to quantify, simulate and forecast risk across one or more hazards.

concepts.name: Sewerage network expansion

concepts.name: Cooling device distribution

concepts.name: Green schoolyard
concepts.definition: Replacing paved school grounds with trees, planting and permeable surfaces to reduce heat and runoff and provide outdoor learning space.

concepts.name: Climate-informed asset management
concepts.definition: Tracking the condition and climate risk exposure of infrastructure assets and incorporating that risk into their planning, maintenance, renewal and investment decisions.

concepts.name: Institutional capacity building
concepts.definition: Training, staffing, data and tooling that strengthen the ability of government institutions to plan and deliver adaptation.

concepts.name: Source water protection
aliases: Sustainable agriculture for source water protection
concepts.definition: Protecting and managing the catchments, recharge areas, wellfields and reservoirs that supply drinking water from pollution and degradation.

concepts.name: Water pipeline renewal

concepts.name: Soil amendment
concepts.definition: Decompacting soils and adding compost, mulch or other organic matter so they absorb and retain more water and better resist drought and erosion.

concepts.name: Mental health support service

concepts.name: Urban ventilation corridor

concepts.name: Controlled-environment agriculture
concepts.definition: Growing food in greenhouses or indoor systems that shield crops from weather extremes and allow conditions to be regulated.

concepts.name: Land raising
concepts.definition: Raising the ground level of a development site or district with fill so that it sits above expected flood levels.

concepts.name: Groundwater level control
aliases: Groundwater level management for flood storage
concepts.definition: Pumping or drainage that lowers a rising groundwater table to protect buildings and infrastructure or to create subsurface flood storage.

concepts.name: Post-disaster psychosocial support
concepts.definition: Psychological first aid, counselling and mental health services provided to people affected by a hazard event in its aftermath.

concepts.name: Heat-responsive urban design
concepts.definition: Guidance and design practice that shape building orientation, massing, street geometry, materials, shading and vegetation so urban form limits heat gain and promotes cooling.

concepts.name: Emergency management information system
concepts.definition: Software and shared data platforms that give responding agencies common situational awareness and coordinate incidents, resources and tasks during an emergency.

concepts.name: Neighbourhood mutual aid network
concepts.definition: Resident-led networks of neighbours who check on, care for and share resources with one another before, during and after hazard events.

concepts.name: Stormwater fee and credit scheme
concepts.definition: An economic instrument of charges, discounts, in-lieu payments or tradable credits tied to a property's runoff that funds drainage and rewards stormwater retention wherever it is most effective.

concepts.name: Decentralised wastewater treatment
concepts.definition: On-site or small-scale systems that treat or safely contain wastewater for a household, building or neighbourhood instead of relying on a central sewer network and plant.

concepts.name: Household water storage
concepts.definition: Tanks or reserves of water kept at household or community level so supply continues through drought, outage or disaster.

concepts.name: Urban waterway pollution control
concepts.definition: Removing debris, litter and pollution from and reducing pollutant discharges to urban lakes, canals, rivers and coastal waters to restore water quality and flow capacity.

concepts.name: Adaptation decision support tool
concepts.definition: A toolkit, GIS platform or software that helps planners analyse options and make adaptation decisions.

concepts.name: Adaptation monitoring and evaluation
concepts.definition: A framework, indicator set or dashboard that tracks the progress and outcomes of adaptation actions and resilience over time.

concepts.name: Adaptation pathways planning
concepts.definition: A planning method that sequences adaptation options over time with defined triggers so decisions can be adjusted as conditions unfold.

concepts.name: Climate-resilient livestock breeding
concepts.definition: Breeding programmes that select or supply livestock breeds tolerant of heat, drought and shifting disease pressure.

concepts.name: Closed containment aquaculture
concepts.definition: Land-based or enclosed recirculating fish and seafood production that shields stock from ocean warming, storms and water quality shocks.

concepts.name: Cool wall
concepts.definition: Facade materials or coatings with high solar reflectance that lower building surface temperature and cooling demand.

concepts.name: Disaster case management
concepts.definition: Assigning caseworkers to affected households to guide them through aid, housing and rebuilding after a hazard event.

concepts.name: Downspout disconnection
concepts.definition: Redirecting roof downspouts from the sewer to lawns, gardens or infiltration areas so roof runoff soaks into the ground.

concepts.name: Grid automation
concepts.definition: Sensors, automated switches and control software that sectionalise the electricity network, isolate faults and reroute power so hazard-caused outages stay small and short.

concepts.name: Port facility hardening
concepts.definition: Raising, strengthening or redesigning docks, piers, berths, marinas and harbour facilities so they withstand surge, waves, storms and sea-level rise.

concepts.name: Public hazard information channel
concepts.definition: A public-facing website, dashboard, screen or display that gives residents current hazard conditions, service status, response and recovery guidance during an emergency.

concepts.name: Public sanitation facility
concepts.definition: Provision of toilets, latrines and washing facilities that give residents safe sanitation and remain usable through floods, droughts and heat.

concepts.name: Sewer rehabilitation
concepts.definition: Sealing, relining or repairing sewer pipes to stop infiltration and leakage and restore capacity.

concepts.name: Stormwater treatment facility

concepts.name: Urban water feature for cooling
concepts.definition: Fountains, ponds, sprays or open water placed in public space to lower local temperature through evaporation and provide relief during heat.

concepts.name: Vegetated pollution buffer

concepts.name: Veterinary service
concepts.definition: Veterinary services and vaccination that protect livestock from diseases and stresses worsened by climate change.

concepts.name: Water control structure upgrade
concepts.definition: Upgrading or modifying weirs, sluices, gates and similar structures so they regulate water levels and flows under larger floods and changed conditions.

concepts.name: Agroforestry
concepts.definition: Integrating trees and shrubs into cropland or pasture to provide shade, soil protection, water retention and diversified yields under climate stress.

concepts.name: Aquatic vegetation restoration
concepts.definition: Conserving or restoring seagrass, kelp and other submerged vegetation that buffer waves, store carbon and support habitat.

concepts.name: Blue roof
concepts.definition: A roof designed to detain rainwater temporarily and release it slowly to reduce runoff peaks.

concepts.name: Building safety inspection
concepts.definition: Inspecting buildings, including rapid assessment after a hazard event, to determine whether they are safe to occupy and what repair is needed.

concepts.name: Channel dredging
concepts.definition: Removing accumulated sediment from river, canal or harbour channels to maintain flow capacity and navigable depth.

concepts.name: Clean air shelter
concepts.definition: A public facility with filtered air where people can take refuge during wildfire smoke or pollution episodes.

concepts.name: Community health worker programme
concepts.definition: Trained local health workers who conduct outreach, check on vulnerable residents and link them to care during climate-related health threats.

concepts.name: Debris flow barrier

concepts.name: Deep pile foundation

concepts.name: Electricity demand response
concepts.definition: Programmes that reduce or shift electricity use at times of peak demand so the grid remains reliable during heat waves and other stress events.

concepts.name: Emergency household sanitation

concepts.name: Emergency water distribution

concepts.name: Floating building

concepts.name: Grassland restoration

concepts.name: Ground-source cooling

concepts.name: Hazardous materials management regulation

concepts.name: Heritage building adaptation

concepts.name: Livelihood diversification

concepts.name: Mobile health service

concepts.name: Multi-utility tunnel

concepts.name: Mutual aid agreement

concepts.name: Open data portal

concepts.definition: A public facility opened during extreme cold for people to warm up and shelter.

concepts.name: Water-retentive pavement
concepts.definition: Paving that holds rainwater in its structure and releases it by evaporation to cool the surface and surrounding air.

concepts.name: Adaptable building design
concepts.definition: Designing buildings so their structure, systems and layouts can be modified cheaply as climate hazards change over their lifetime.

concepts.name: Adaptation cost-benefit analysis
concepts.definition: Economic appraisal that compares the costs and avoided losses of adaptation options to prioritise investment.

concepts.name: Adjustable in-channel weir
concepts.definition: A movable or inflatable dam within a river or canal channel that is raised or lowered to regulate water levels for flood and drought management.

concepts.name: Alternative building material
concepts.definition: Using local, alternative or innovative construction materials and methods in place of conventional ones to improve hazard resistance or affordability.

concepts.name: Atmospheric water capture
concepts.definition: Harvesting water from fog, dew or humid air as a supplementary supply.

concepts.name: Building massing step-back
concepts.definition: Design rules that step back upper floors or shape building bulk so streets receive wind, daylight and ventilation that reduce heat.

concepts.name: Building retrofit technical assistance
concepts.definition: Advisory services that help owners assess and carry out hazard-resistant building retrofits.

concepts.name: Climate information service
concepts.definition: Tailored weather and climate forecasts delivered to specific users such as farmers, utilities or responders to support decisions.

concepts.name: Climate-adapted plant selection
concepts.definition: Choosing tree and plant species and provenances for public planting that will tolerate projected heat, drought, pests and storms.

concepts.name: Cold weather emergency response programme
concepts.definition: Coordinated response to extreme cold events, including outreach to vulnerable people, warnings and activation of shelter.

concepts.name: Community asset mapping
concepts.definition: Mapping the facilities, networks and resources a community can draw on during hazard events.

concepts.name: Community volunteer programme
concepts.definition: Recruiting, organising and supporting resident volunteers who assist with preparedness, response and recovery tasks.

concepts.name: Condensate recovery
concepts.definition: Capturing water that condenses from air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment for non-potable reuse.

concepts.name: Continuous pressurised water supply
concepts.definition: Upgrading a piped water system from intermittent to continuous pressurised supply so households have reliable water during heat and drought.

concepts.name: Crowdsourced disaster response
concepts.definition: Platforms that let residents report needs and volunteer resources during a hazard event to coordinate response.

concepts.name: Disaster animal sheltering
concepts.definition: Sheltering, evacuating and reuniting pets and livestock with owners during and after a hazard event.

concepts.name: Emergency assembly point
concepts.definition: A designated safe location where people gather during an evacuation or hazard event.

concepts.name: Emergency firefighting water supply
concepts.definition: Dedicated hydrants, tanks or reservoirs that guarantee water for firefighting during wildfire or supply failure.

concepts.name: Emergency fuel supply
concepts.definition: Reserves and distribution arrangements that keep fuel available for emergency services and critical operations during a disruption.

concepts.name: Emergency helpline
concepts.definition: A staffed telephone or messaging line that residents can contact for help, information and referral during and after hazard events.

concepts.name: Emergency preparedness kit
concepts.definition: Distributing or promoting kits of supplies that households keep ready for hazard events.

concepts.name: Environmental flow management
concepts.definition: Releasing or reserving water in rivers to keep ecosystems functioning during drought and altered flow.

concepts.name: Equity screening tool
concepts.definition: A procedure that checks plans, projects or investments for their effects on vulnerable and disadvantaged groups before approval.

concepts.name: Faecal sludge management service
concepts.definition: Services that safely empty, transport and treat sludge from pit latrines and septic tanks so flooding does not spread contamination.

concepts.name: Farmer training and extension
concepts.definition: Training, advisory and extension services that build farmers' skills and productivity under changing climate conditions.

concepts.name: Floating debris barrier
concepts.definition: A boom or screen across a waterway that catches floating debris before it blocks drains, bridges or intakes during floods.

concepts.name: Flood diversion channel
concepts.definition: An engineered canal or channel that diverts floodwater away from a protected area to a safe outlet.

concepts.name: Flood-aware navigation application
concepts.definition: A mobile or in-vehicle application that routes travellers around flooded or closed roads using real-time flood data.

concepts.name: Flood-responsive traffic management
concepts.definition: Closing, rerouting and signalling roads in real time when flooding is forecast or detected so traffic avoids inundated sections.

concepts.name: Food supply diversification
concepts.definition: Widening the range of sources and routes from which food is supplied so that supply continues when one source or route is disrupted.

concepts.name: Green area ratio requirement
concepts.definition: A planning rule requiring a minimum share of vegetated or permeable surface on development sites.

concepts.name: Gross pollutant trap
concepts.definition: A structure in a stormwater drain or channel that captures litter, debris and coarse sediment before runoff reaches waterways or blocks downstream drainage.

concepts.name: Groundwater monitoring
concepts.definition: A network of wells and sensors that track groundwater levels and quality to manage drought, flooding and abstraction.

concepts.name: Groundwater remediation
concepts.definition: Cleaning up contaminated aquifers so that stored groundwater can serve as a drought-resilient supply.

concepts.name: Harmful algal bloom control
concepts.definition: Measures that prevent, monitor and treat harmful algal blooms in lakes, reservoirs and coastal waters.

concepts.name: Hazard remediation workforce training
concepts.definition: Training workers to safely clean up, remediate and restore sites after floods, fires and other hazard events.

concepts.name: Hazard risk disclosure
concepts.definition: Informing property owners and buyers of the climate hazard risk of their building or site.

concepts.name: Hazard-resistant construction material
concepts.definition: Use of building materials that resist flood, wind, heat or fire damage in new construction and retrofit.

concepts.name: Hazard-resistant roofing
concepts.definition: Strengthening, strapping or replacing roofs so they withstand high wind, hail and heavy rain without failure.

concepts.name: Heat-mitigating parking lot design
concepts.definition: Designing or retrofitting parking lots with shade, reflective or permeable surfaces and planting to lower surface temperature and runoff.

concepts.name: Household savings scheme
concepts.definition: Organised savings groups or accounts that help households build financial reserves to absorb climate shocks.

concepts.name: IT continuity and data redundancy
concepts.definition: Redundant data centres, backups and continuity arrangements that keep digital services running through hazard events.

concepts.name: Indoor moisture and mould control
concepts.definition: Ventilation, dehumidification and remediation measures that prevent damp and mould in buildings affected by flooding, humidity or heat.

concepts.name: Mobile wastewater treatment unit
concepts.definition: A transportable treatment unit that provides sanitation where fixed works fail or are absent during a hazard event.

concepts.name: Native vegetation restoration
concepts.definition: Re-establishing native plant communities on degraded land to restore habitat, hold soil and buffer climate extremes.

concepts.name: On-site stormwater retention requirement
concepts.definition: A regulation requiring new or redeveloped sites to retain or detain a set volume of runoff on the property.

concepts.name: Passive irrigation
concepts.definition: Directing stormwater runoff into tree pits and planting beds so vegetation is watered without piped irrigation.

concepts.name: Personal emergency plan
concepts.definition: Helping vulnerable residents prepare individual plans for evacuation, medication, support and contacts during hazard events.

concepts.name: Plan integration scorecard
concepts.definition: A scoring tool that evaluates how consistently resilience and hazard reduction are integrated across a jurisdiction's plans and policies.

concepts.name: Pollinator habitat
concepts.definition: Plantings that provide food and shelter for pollinators to sustain ecosystems and food production under climate stress.

concepts.name: Proactive rental housing inspection
concepts.definition: Routine inspection of rental housing to confirm it meets habitability standards for heat, damp and hazard safety before tenants are harmed.

concepts.name: Property resilience audit
concepts.definition: An on-site assessment of an individual property that identifies its hazard exposure and recommends specific retrofit measures to the owner.

concepts.name: Public handwashing station
concepts.definition: Handwashing facilities installed in public spaces so people can maintain hygiene during heat, disease outbreaks and post-disaster conditions.

concepts.name: Rapid post-disaster damage assessment
concepts.definition: Quick field or remote survey of damage after a hazard event to guide response, recovery and aid.

concepts.name: Reservoir capacity expansion
concepts.definition: Enlarging or adding raw-water storage reservoirs so that supply can be carried through longer dry periods.

concepts.name: Resilience observatory
concepts.definition: A standing unit or platform that collects, analyses and publishes indicators on hazards, vulnerability and adaptation progress to inform decisions.

concepts.name: Resilient infrastructure design standard
concepts.definition: Design standards that require roads, utilities and other infrastructure to be built to withstand projected climate hazards.

concepts.name: Sediment control
concepts.definition: Basins, traps and practices that capture sediment carried by runoff before it clogs drains, channels and reservoirs.

concepts.name: Seismic monitoring network
concepts.definition: Instruments that detect and report ground motion to support earthquake warning and response.

concepts.name: Snow and ice management
concepts.definition: Clearing, de-icing and storage operations that keep roads, transit and services functioning during snow and ice events.

concepts.name: Social cohesion programme
concepts.definition: Activities that strengthen neighbourly ties and local networks so communities support each other during hazard events.

concepts.name: Social media emergency monitoring
concepts.definition: A platform that scans social media during hazard events to detect incidents, needs and misinformation for situational awareness.

concepts.name: Stormwater tree trench
concepts.definition: A row of street trees planted in a connected underground trench of structural soil or stone that stores and infiltrates runoff.

concepts.name: Street watering
concepts.definition: Spraying water on road and pavement surfaces during heat so that evaporation lowers surface and air temperature.

concepts.name: Telemedicine
concepts.definition: Remote delivery of health consultations and care so that patients keep access to medical services when travel or facilities are disrupted by hazards.

concepts.name: Temporary medical facility
concepts.definition: Field hospitals or temporary clinics set up to treat people when a hazard event overwhelms or disables health facilities.

concepts.name: Temporary post-disaster housing
concepts.definition: Interim housing for displaced households in the months after a hazard event until permanent housing is available.

concepts.name: Transport network redundancy
concepts.definition: Providing alternative routes, links or modes so that movement of people and goods continues when part of the transport network is disrupted by a hazard.

concepts.name: Underground flood storage facility
concepts.definition: A below-ground structure such as a parking garage or vault designed to hold stormwater temporarily during heavy rain.

concepts.name: Urban development monitoring
concepts.definition: Using satellite or aerial imagery to track land cover change and construction so that encroachment into hazard zones and loss of green cover can be detected.

concepts.name: Urban microclimate modelling
concepts.definition: Simulating street- and district-scale temperature, wind and radiation to test how design and greening options change local heat conditions.

concepts.name: Vulnerable population registry
concepts.definition: A maintained register and map of medically or socially vulnerable residents used to target outreach and assistance during hazard events.

concepts.name: Water audit
concepts.definition: A systematic account of water use and losses in a building, utility or sector to identify savings.

concepts.name: Water trading
concepts.definition: A market mechanism that lets water entitlements be bought and sold so supply is reallocated during scarcity.
